note: Bands for scripts/crash-suite.js. Every band is from docs/CRASH-REFERENCES.md, whose ids the sources name, never from the plant. Confidence HIGH, MED or LOW as that file grades it.

q5-gate-15.refStill: A 5 inch racer clips a 1 inch PVC gate upright with one arm: the struck prop bends or snaps, the quad spins away from the pole and tumbles to the grass several metres on, frame whole.

q5-gate-30.refStill: The same clip at race speed: props on the struck side gone, an arm possibly snapped at the motor, the quad cartwheels 10 to 60 m down the course, battery still strapped on.

q5-wall.refStill: Square into masonry at full speed: every prop gone, an arm broken, the camera knocked askew or out of its mount, the battery often thrown; the quad drops at the foot of the wall.

checks.source: R-ARM (320 to 719 J over 15 to 40 mm)

q5-prop-strike.refStill: A hard landing on a bank: one pair of blade tips hits the grass, the props chip or bend, the quad slaps down upright where it landed.

checks.source: R-A3-DROP (a Phantom leg failed at 10.1 m/s, this is under half that)

q5-slope.refStill: Into a grass hillside: the quad bounces and tumbles down the slope over several contacts, props breaking one by one, and stops well down it.

checks.source: R-A4-REBOUND (6.5 to 8.4 m per rebound at 20 m/s, 30 deg; scaled by v squared)

q5-branch.refStill: An arm catches a thin branch: the struck prop is chewed, the quad spins off the branch and drops near the tree.

q5-inverted.refStill: Upside down onto the grass at walking pace: nothing breaks, it lies on its back, and turtle mode rolls it over (less reliably on long grass).

checks.source: R-TURTLE (turtle recovers on flat ground; the contact self-test proof is crossing out of inverted)

q5-prop-loss.refStill: A prop leaves at speed: the quad yaws into a fast spin, cannot hold attitude and falls out of the sky.

checks.imposed: the scenario breaks it (sim_part_break); this checks the break took

checks.source: R-PROPLOSS (from 10 m: free fall is 1.4 s, a partly thrusting spin longer)

whoop-wall.refStill: A 65 mm whoop bumps a wall at a brisk walk: it bounces off, wobbles and keeps flying, nothing damaged.

checks.source: R-WHOOP, docs/CRASH-PLAN.md (a whoop is built to survive this)

whoop-floor.refStill: Dropped onto the floor from head height: a bounce, it stays upright or flips, the pilot punches out and flies on.

whoop-gate.refStill: Full speed into a gate side: the duct takes it, the whoop tumbles a metre or two to the floor, perhaps a chipped blade, frame and motors whole.

sky-stall.refStill: Stalled low with the stick back: a wing or the nose drops and it hits nose low; the foam nose crushes, and it stops on its nose or flops onto its back within a couple of metres.

checks.source: R-A14-FOAM (a pusher prop is behind the crumple zone)
R-A14-FOAM (foam pusher 0.30 to 0.34 g/ft lbf on the head, puller about 3 times), R-FOAM crush check
R-C172 (nose down into soft ground, pivots and ends inverted)

sky-nose-in.refStill: A full power dive into the ground: the nose section snaps off at the battery bay, the wings fold or come off at the root, motor and battery tumble on; wreckage within a few metres of the hole.

checks.source: R-A14-FOAM (eBee+ nose broke off from 7.6 m/s on a rigid target), R-A3-PARTS
R-A3-PARTS, R-A4-REBOUND (fixed wing rebound 0.03 to 0.2 of impact speed)

sky-cartwheel.refStill: A banked low pass catches a wingtip: the aircraft pivots on it and cartwheels, one to three rotations, the tip crushed and the prop broken, ending on its back or side.

checks.source: R-AFH (cartwheels: at least onto its back once)

sky-belly-fast.refStill: Belly landed at twice the stall: a slap, a long slide across the grass, upright and undamaged.

checks.source: R-C172 test 1, R-A14-FOAM (foam belly landings are routine)
R-SLIDE (v squared over 2 mu g, mu 0.3 to 0.6)

sky-pole.refStill: A wing hits a wooden pole at cruise: the leading edge crushes and the panel folds or snaps at the pole, the aircraft whips round it and drops at its foot.

checks.source: R-AFH (asymmetric contact, the loss of one wing), R-FOAM

sky-tree.refStill: Into a tree crown at cruise: branches decelerate it over a metre or two, skin torn, prop broken, and it hangs in the branches.

checks.source: R-AFH trees, R-SLOWSTICK (stuck in a tree, torn wing)
R-AFH ("considerable cushioning and braking effect without destroying the airplane")
R-AFH ("hang the airplane in the tree branches")

checks.source: R-A14-FOAM (puller prop, spinner and motor at the nose)

R-C172 (nose down into soft ground, pivots and ends inverted)

cub-nose-over.refStill: Pushed tail up too early at full power: the tail rises, the nose tips forward over the wheels, the prop digs into the grass and chips or snaps, and it stops standing on its nose or flips onto its back within about its own length.

checks.source: R-NOSEOVER (a tailwheel aircraft has nothing to stop it nosing over except the propeller; a nose over is a prop strike)
R-NOSEOVER (a nose over from a take off roll; the damage in the reports is the prop, and the fin and rudder when it goes onto its back), R-FOAM
R-NOSEOVER (AFH: tipping up onto its nose; the tendency grows until it flips; NTSB: nosed over and came to rest inverted)
R-NOSEOVER, DERIVED (it pivots over the main wheels, so the CG moves about its own length at most)

checks.source: R-SLOWSTICK ("Almost every landing so far has been a shallow or steep dive into the weeds. The plane holds up well to these landings")
R-SLIDE, DERIVED (the most it can arrive with is 4.84 m/s plus a 1 m drop without drag, 6.6 m/s; a foam belly on grass at mu 0.3 slides v squared over 2 mu g, 7.4 m, the farthest a nose in can go)

checks.source: R-CHUTE (4.1 to 4.6 m/s rated, 5.5 m/s floor, rates of descent: the vertical speed at touchdown, not the wind's drift)
R-CHUTE drag (dragged 5 to 100 m without a release above about 3 m/s of wind)

bramor-catapult-stall.refStill: Off the rail too slow: it pitches up, stalls, drops a wing and goes in nose first some metres ahead of the catapult.

timberf-nose-dig.refStill: Touched down nose low: the float bows dig in, the tail comes over and the aircraft flips onto its back, hanging upside down from its floats.

checks.source: R-TSB ("inverted in the water, suspended by the floats")

timberf-float-catch.refStill: A fast turn on the step: the outside float buries, the wingtip goes in and the aircraft waterloops over onto its side or back.

timberf-capsize.refStill: A gust across the lake lifts the upwind wing, the downwind float buries and the aircraft rolls over onto its back.

checks.source: R-SEAPLANE ("tipping could continue until the seaplane capsizes"), R-TSB

timberf-porpoise.refStill: Held nose high on the step: it rocks bow to stern, each cycle worse, leaves the water too slow, stalls and drops back in.

checks.source: R-SEAPLANE ("each oscillation becomes increasingly severe"; 2 to 4 cycles uncorrected, an estimate)
R-SEAPLANE ("premature lift-off with an extremely high angle of attack")
